newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares dive on corruption scandal - traders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares dive on corruption scandal - traders.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended the first half of today's session sharply lower after a newspaper linked a government minister to an alleged cash-for-votes scam involving a re-election bill, brokers said.
The Bovespa index plunged 3.24 percent to 10,303 points shortly before the one-hour lunch break.
Only electronic trade is carried on during lunch.
Market turnover was 564.8 million reais ($532.8 million) and some traders say it may reach a heavy one billion reais.
Benchmark Telebras preferred led the market's drop, plunging 3.55 percent to 130.40 reais, while its common stock lost 3.51 percent 123.50 reais.

The bolsa's nosedive was triggered by a Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper report today alleging that Communications Minister Sergio Motta was involved in a vote-buying scheme to get a bill allowing re-election for president, governors and mayors approved by deputies.
The scandal erupted Tuesday when Folha reported that five deputies from the northern state of Acre allegedly received money to vote in favor of the bill.

Although government officials said the scandal will not slow the voting of the reforms in Congress, traders remain concerned that a threat of a congressional inquiry into the vote-buying scheme could delay key votes.
They also fear what Folha de Sao Paulo, which published the reports Tuesday and Wednesday, will bring in its Thursday's edition.
The market ignored the fact that a Senate panel rejected changes to the re-election amendment, allowing it to go to the full Senate.
Analysts said the scandal also prompted investors to take profits as the bolsa has "fat to burn" after recent strong rises.
They said they hope the market will rebound somewhat later in the day on some bargain-hunting.
"Some shares will be very attractive and investors should return to the market to take advantage of the prices," one trader said.
